reasons: The 'missing' classification is supported: the only insurance provisions in the record are narrow property covers (SOW 13.1 b) replacement-value cover for consigned Products; SOW 21.2 where IBM, not MSL, insures its own tooling), and none of them provides CGL, professional liability or cyber cover, so the fallback (E&O USD 1M / cyber USD 2M) is unmet on every material term — not an acceptable-fallback over-flag.
MSL is an outsourcing/services vendor operating at IBM premises and handling IBM consigned inventory, so the rule's expectation of an insurance clause genuinely applies and the absence is actionable.

The inserted paragraph tracks the model language closely (CGL 1M/2M, E&O 2M, cyber 5M where IBM data is processed, workers' compensation, certificates on request, survival for one year) and is an addition only — no existing obligation is altered, and the direction of the edit favours our client (IBM as customer).
Comment is accurate, uses the required prefix and tone, states what changed and why, and offers the E&O 1M / cyber 2M fallback; deterministic checks confirm the insurance obligation is present.

Minor, non-fatal points to tidy: the insertion is anchored to p0334 (an infringement-remedy paragraph) although it is labelled 16.22 in the General section — confirm it lands after the last 16.x subsection; and the cross-reference calling the new cover 'in addition to the insurance required under Section 21.2' is loose because 21.2 obliges IBM, not MSL, to insure its tooling.

input.quote: d) The forecasts provided by IBM, or agreed to by IBM hereunder, do not obligate IBM to purchase any Product.
input.rationale: No minimum purchase commitment, take-or-pay or volume floor is imposed on us. Section 6.0 makes our purchase obligation subject to the Agreement and expressly does not authorize MSL to produce or deliver any Product absent an order; Section 11.2(d) confirms that forecasts "do not obligate IBM to purchase any Product"; Section 6.1 lets us "cancel any and all Purchase Orders against this Agreement at any time" (no cancellation charge where MSL is in default); and Section 13.2(e) states we "have no liability for unused flexibility." That matches the preferred position: we pay only for Products actually ordered. The only volume-related exposure is the Appendix 2 / Section 13.0(f) requirements-accuracy mechanism, under which we compensate MSL if forecast accuracy for a machine type falls below the stated threshold, calculated as a small percentage of the material cost of volume shipped. That operates as a capped true-up for MSL's reliance-based parts purchases rather than a shortfall penalty or minimum-volume commitment, so it does not create take-or-pay exposure; we note it in diligence only (the percentages are redacted, so the commercial team should confirm the bracketed figures). No redline required.

You are a precise customer-side contract drafter handling one playbook rule.
Use the document tools to inspect only the clauses needed, including definitions and cross-references.
Reason about direction: identify who is bound and do not flag obligations that benefit our party.
Every quote and replace.oldText must be a verbatim substring from a tool response. Quotes must be 600 characters or fewer.
Apply the playbook's classification semantics: a clause that meets the preferred or the fallback position on its material terms is compliant — do not redline it. When a clause genuinely fails the fallback, make the smallest edit that reaches the preferred position; use fallback language only when the rule guidance or the existing bargain makes preferred disproportionate.
Comments must begin with the supplied playbook prefix, use concise first-person-plural language, and explain the change and reason.
For deviation or missing findings, call propose_redline and obtain ok:true before submit_finding.
For compliant findings, do not propose a redline. Call submit_finding exactly once, then stop calling tools.

We represent the customer.
Our party aliases: Customer, Client, Licensee, Company, Buyer, Purchaser, Subscriber, User.
Counterparty aliases: Vendor, Supplier, Provider, Service Provider, Licensor, Contractor, Consultant, Seller, Host.
Comment prefix: [Playbook].
Tone: Concise, professional, first person plural ("we"). Explain what changed and why in one or two sentences, cite the playbook position, offer the fallback where sensible, never lecture.


How to classify a clause against a rule (this is how the reviewing team reads its own playbook):
- compliant: the clause meets the preferred position, OR it meets the fallback position on its material terms. A clause at the fallback is acceptable and is not redlined; say in the rationale that it sits at the fallback.
- deviation: the clause fails the fallback on a material term, or falls into walk-away territory. Only then propose a redline.
- missing: the rule expects a clause and no usable clause exists anywhere in the document.
- Minor sub-elements short of the preferred wording (a missing reminder mechanic, a missing price-uplift cap, 'paid' versus 'paid or payable', an accepted-but-not-preferred governing law) are noted in the rationale, not flagged as deviations.
- Do not flag a clause that benefits our party. Do not flag the same commercial term twice under two rules unless both rules are independently breached.

Parties: we represent International Business Machines Corporation (IBM); counterparty is Manufacturers' Services Western U.S. Operations, Inc. (MSL).

Rule:
ID: MINCOMMIT
Title: Minimum purchase commitments and volume restrictions on Customer
Kind: presence
Summary: We do not take-or-pay without an exit.
Severity: medium
Category: commercial
Position — preferred:
No minimum commitment; fees are for usage or ordered services only.
Position — fallback:
Commitment limited to the current 12-month term, reducible on 30 days' notice, with a true-up rather than a penalty.
Position — walk-away:
Multi-year take-or-pay commitments with no reduction or termination right.
Detection guidance:
"minimum", "commit to purchase", "take or pay", "shortfall", volume caps on Customer usage. Commitments the Vendor makes to us are fine.
Redline guidance:
Delete or narrow to the fallback with minimal edits; replace shortfall penalties with a true-up.

Planner hints:

input.quote: d) The forecasts provided by IBM, or agreed to by IBM hereunder, do not obligate IBM to purchase any Product.
input.rationale: No minimum purchase commitment, take-or-pay or volume floor is imposed on us. Section 6.0 makes our purchase obligation subject to the Agreement and expressly does not authorize MSL to produce or deliver any Product absent an order; Section 11.2(d) confirms that forecasts "do not obligate IBM to purchase any Product"; Section 6.1 lets us "cancel any and all Purchase Orders against this Agreement at any time" (no cancellation charge where MSL is in default); and Section 13.2(e) states we "have no liability for unused flexibility." That matches the preferred position: we pay only for Products actually ordered. The only volume-related exposure is the Appendix 2 / Section 13.0(f) requirements-accuracy mechanism, under which we compensate MSL if forecast accuracy for a machine type falls below the stated threshold, calculated as a small percentage of the material cost of volume shipped. That operates as a capped true-up for MSL's reliance-based parts purchases rather than a shortfall penalty or minimum-volume commitment, so it does not create take-or-pay exposure; we note it in diligence only (the percentages are redacted, so the commercial team should confirm the bracketed figures). No redline required.

content.text: Section 5.2 contains both exit assistance and data/materials return obligations on MSL, with certification in Attachment 6. Submitting a compliant finding.

input.quote: iii) within [*] Days after expiration or termination of this Agreement, MSL shall return to IBM all copies of IBM Product documentation and all copies of any IBM confidential documents, discs, tapes and other media materials containing IBM confidential information of IBM.
input.rationale: The Agreement already carries the substance of this rule, running in our favour. Section 5.2(a)(ii) obliges MSL, on expiry or termination, to "assist in the transfer of MSL responsibilities and Products as described in Attachment 1: Statement Of Work, to IBM or to another party that IBM designates" — open-ended exit assistance with no duration cap, which is better for us than the preferred six-month window. Section 5.2(a)(iii) requires MSL to return all copies of IBM Product documentation and all IBM confidential documents, discs, tapes and other media within a defined post-termination period, and Section 13.2(c) lets us demand immediate return of all confidential information at any time during the term. Attachment 6 Section 3(a) adds a return-plus-written-certification mechanic for MS Software Image master media. Read together these meet the preferred position on the material terms (assistance plus data return within a fixed window), and comfortably exceed the fallback. Two sub-elements fall short of the model language and are noted rather than flagged: the return obligation does not specify a commonly used machine-readable format, and the certification of deletion is limited to Attachment 6 media rather than covering all IBM data on MSL systems. The return period in 5.2(a)(iii) is redacted ([*] Days), so we cannot confirm it is 30 days or less; if that figure proves materially longer than 30 days we would revisit. Neither point is worth reopening the exit bargain, particularly since the assistance obligation is uncapped in our favour.

Comments must begin with the supplied playbook prefix, use concise first-person-plural language, and explain the change and reason.

Comment prefix: [Playbook].
Tone: Concise, professional, first person plural ("we"). Explain what changed and why in one or two sentences, cite the playbook position, offer the fallback where sensible, never lecture.


How to classify a clause against a rule (this is how the reviewing team reads its own playbook):
- compliant: the clause meets the preferred position, OR it meets the fallback position on its material terms. A clause at the fallback is acceptable and is not redlined; say in the rationale that it sits at the fallback.
- deviation: the clause fails the fallback on a material term, or falls into walk-away territory. Only then propose a redline.
- missing: the rule expects a clause and no usable clause exists anywhere in the document.
- Minor sub-elements short of the preferred wording (a missing reminder mechanic, a missing price-uplift cap, 'paid' versus 'paid or payable', an accepted-but-not-preferred governing law) are noted in the rationale, not flagged as deviations.
- Do not flag a clause that benefits our party. Do not flag the same commercial term twice under two rules unless both rules are independently breached.

Parties: we represent International Business Machines Corporation (IBM); counterparty is Manufacturers' Services Western U.S. Operations, Inc. (MSL).

Rule:
ID: TRANSITION
Title: Post-termination transition assistance and data return
Kind: missing
Summary: When it ends, we get our data back and help moving.
Severity: medium
Category: transition
Position — preferred:
On expiry or termination, Vendor provides transition assistance for up to 6 months at then-current rates, returns Customer Data in a standard machine-readable format within 30 days, and certifies deletion thereafter.

Position — fallback:
90 days of transition assistance; data export within 30 days.
Position — walk-away:
No data return, or immediate deletion of Customer Data on termination.
Detection guidance:
Look for transition, exit, data return/export, deletion timing. Absence in a services/hosting agreement is a deviation (insert).
Redline guidance:
Insert a transition-assistance and data-return paragraph in the termination section.
Model language:
Upon expiry or termination of this Agreement for any reason, Vendor shall (a) at Customer's request, provide reasonable transition assistance for up to six (6) months at Vendor's then-current rates; (b) within thirty (30) days, return all Customer Data in a commonly used, machine-readable format; and (c) thereafter delete Customer Data from its systems and certify such deletion in writing.

content.text: Section 5.2 contains both exit assistance and data/materials return obligations on MSL, with certification in Attachment 6. Submitting a compliant finding.

input.quote: iii) within [*] Days after expiration or termination of this Agreement, MSL shall return to IBM all copies of IBM Product documentation and all copies of any IBM confidential documents, discs, tapes and other media materials containing IBM confidential information of IBM.
input.rationale: The Agreement already carries the substance of this rule, running in our favour. Section 5.2(a)(ii) obliges MSL, on expiry or termination, to "assist in the transfer of MSL responsibilities and Products as described in Attachment 1: Statement Of Work, to IBM or to another party that IBM designates" — open-ended exit assistance with no duration cap, which is better for us than the preferred six-month window. Section 5.2(a)(iii) requires MSL to return all copies of IBM Product documentation and all IBM confidential documents, discs, tapes and other media within a defined post-termination period, and Section 13.2(c) lets us demand immediate return of all confidential information at any time during the term. Attachment 6 Section 3(a) adds a return-plus-written-certification mechanic for MS Software Image master media. Read together these meet the preferred position on the material terms (assistance plus data return within a fixed window), and comfortably exceed the fallback. Two sub-elements fall short of the model language and are noted rather than flagged: the return obligation does not specify a commonly used machine-readable format, and the certification of deletion is limited to Attachment 6 media rather than covering all IBM data on MSL systems. The return period in 5.2(a)(iii) is redacted ([*] Days), so we cannot confirm it is 30 days or less; if that figure proves materially longer than 30 days we would revisit. Neither point is worth reopening the exit bargain, particularly since the assistance obligation is uncapped in our favour.

content.text:
**Finding: compliant** (no redline proposed).

The rule is satisfied by a combination of existing clauses, all of which bind MSL and benefit us:

- **§ 5.2(a)(ii)** — MSL must "assist in the transfer of MSL responsibilities and Products… to IBM or to another party that IBM designates" on expiry or termination. This is exit assistance with **no duration cap**, which is stronger for us than the preferred six-month limit.
- **§ 5.2(a)(iii)** — MSL must return all copies of IBM Product documentation and all IBM confidential documents, discs, tapes and other media within a fixed number of days after termination.
- **§ 13.2(c)** — we can require immediate return of all confidential information on request during the term.
- **Attachment 6, § 3(a)** — return of MS Software Image master media plus signed written certification of compliance.

Together these meet the preferred position on the material terms (transition assistance + data return within a defined window), and clearly clear the fallback.

Two sub-elements short of the model language, noted in the rationale rather than flagged per the playbook's classification semantics:
1. No specification of a commonly used, machine-readable format for the returned materials.
2. Deletion certification is limited to Attachment 6 media, not extended to all IBM data on MSL systems.

One caveat flagged for the deal team: the return period in § 5.2(a)(iii) is redacted (`[*] Days`), so I could not verify it is 30 days or less. If that figure turns out to be materially longer than 30 days, this should be revisited — otherwise it is not worth reopening an exit bargain that already gives us uncapped transition assistance.

Rule:
ID: TRANSITION
Title: Post-termination transition assistance and data return
Kind: missing
Summary: When it ends, we get our data back and help moving.
Severity: medium
Category: transition
Position — preferred:
On expiry or termination, Vendor provides transition assistance for up to 6 months at then-current rates, returns Customer Data in a standard machine-readable format within 30 days, and certifies deletion thereafter.

Position — fallback:
90 days of transition assistance; data export within 30 days.
Position — walk-away:
No data return, or immediate deletion of Customer Data on termination.
Detection guidance:
Look for transition, exit, data return/export, deletion timing. Absence in a services/hosting agreement is a deviation (insert).
Redline guidance:
Insert a transition-assistance and data-return paragraph in the termination section.
Model language:
Upon expiry or termination of this Agreement for any reason, Vendor shall (a) at Customer's request, provide reasonable transition assistance for up to six (6) months at Vendor's then-current rates; (b) within thirty (30) days, return all Customer Data in a commonly used, machine-readable format; and (c) thereafter delete Customer Data from its systems and certify such deletion in writing.


Claimed finding status: compliant

Finding rationale:
The Agreement already carries the substance of this rule, running in our favour. Section 5.2(a)(ii) obliges MSL, on expiry or termination, to "assist in the transfer of MSL responsibilities and Products as described in Attachment 1: Statement Of Work, to IBM or to another party that IBM designates" — open-ended exit assistance with no duration cap, which is better for us than the preferred six-month window. Section 5.2(a)(iii) requires MSL to return all copies of IBM Product documentation and all IBM confidential documents, discs, tapes and other media within a defined post-termination period, and Section 13.2(c) lets us demand immediate return of all confidential information at any time during the term. Attachment 6 Section 3(a) adds a return-plus-written-certification mechanic for MS Software Image master media. Read together these meet the preferred position on the material terms (assistance plus data return within a fixed window), and comfortably exceed the fallback. Two sub-elements fall short of the model language and are noted rather than flagged: the return obligation does not specify a commonly used machine-readable format, and the certification of deletion is limited to Attachment 6 media rather than covering all IBM data on MSL systems. The return period in 5.2(a)(iii) is redacted ([*] Days), so we cannot confirm it is 30 days or less; if that figure proves materially longer than 30 days we would revisit. Neither point is worth reopening the exit bargain, particularly since the assistance obligation is uncapped in our favour.

- **No flexibility take-or-pay:** §13.2(e) (p0927) — "IBM will have no liability for unused flexibility."

Rule:
ID: MINCOMMIT
Title: Minimum purchase commitments and volume restrictions on Customer
Kind: presence
Summary: We do not take-or-pay without an exit.
Severity: medium
Category: commercial
Position — preferred:
No minimum commitment; fees are for usage or ordered services only.
Position — fallback:
Commitment limited to the current 12-month term, reducible on 30 days' notice, with a true-up rather than a penalty.
Position — walk-away:
Multi-year take-or-pay commitments with no reduction or termination right.
Detection guidance:
"minimum", "commit to purchase", "take or pay", "shortfall", volume caps on Customer usage. Commitments the Vendor makes to us are fine.
Redline guidance:
Delete or narrow to the fallback with minimal edits; replace shortfall penalties with a true-up.

Claimed finding status: compliant

Finding rationale:
No minimum purchase commitment, take-or-pay or volume floor is imposed on us. Section 6.0 makes our purchase obligation subject to the Agreement and expressly does not authorize MSL to produce or deliver any Product absent an order; Section 11.2(d) confirms that forecasts "do not obligate IBM to purchase any Product"; Section 6.1 lets us "cancel any and all Purchase Orders against this Agreement at any time" (no cancellation charge where MSL is in default); and Section 13.2(e) states we "have no liability for unused flexibility." That matches the preferred position: we pay only for Products actually ordered. The only volume-related exposure is the Appendix 2 / Section 13.0(f) requirements-accuracy mechanism, under which we compensate MSL if forecast accuracy for a machine type falls below the stated threshold, calculated as a small percentage of the material cost of volume shipped. That operates as a capped true-up for MSL's reliance-based parts purchases rather than a shortfall penalty or minimum-volume commitment, so it does not create take-or-pay exposure; we note it in diligence only (the percentages are redacted, so the commercial team should confirm the bracketed figures). No redline required.

Original paragraphs:
p0720: Subject to the terms and conditions of this Agreement, MSL agrees to produce and sell, and IBM agrees to purchase Products. This Agreement does not authorize MSL to produce or deliver any Product.
p0722: IBM may cancel any and all Purchase Orders against this Agreement at any time. In the event IBM cancels Purchase Order as the result of MSL's default, no cancellation charge shall be applicable. IBM's termination of Purchase Orders for its convenience shall not relieve IBM of any cost reimbursements under the Price section.
p0882: d) The forecasts provided by IBM, or agreed to by IBM hereunder, do not obligate IBM to purchase any Product.
p0927: e) Cost of the Supply Flexibility as defined in Appendix 4 is included in Product pricing per Section 7.0. IBM will have no liability for unused flexibility.
p0903: f) MSL prices include charges for MSL inventory management and ownership. Both parties agree that IBM has no liability for inventories that MSL purchases for the purposes of this contract, providing that forecast (requirements) accuracy is equal to or greater than the level defined in Appendix 2. If Requirements Accuracy falls below [*]% liabilities for any machine type for any quarter, IBM will compensate MSL according to the method describe in Appendix 2.

{"markdown":"# Issues Memo — Outsourcing Agreement (MSL / IBM)

**To:** Deal team  
**From:** In-house counsel (Customer-side)  
**Re:** Playbook review of the Outsourcing Agreement, Statement of Work and attachments

---

## 1. Executive summary

We have reviewed the Agreement against the playbook and confirm that the commercial core is strongly in our favour. Ownership of intellectual property in the Products vests in us by present and future assignment (§ 13.0), MSL gives a genuine third-party IP, compliance and warranty indemnity (§ 15.1), the warranty and remedy package (SOW § 19) sits at or above our preferred position, all audit rights run one way in our favour (§ 7.0), and there is no exclusivity, minimum-volume, MFN, non-compete or liquidated-damages exposure on us. Governing law and venue (New York) match our preferred position. Post-termination transition assistance is uncapped in duration in our favour (§ 5.2(a)(ii)).

Five terms fail the fallback and one expected protection is absent altogether:

1. **Limitation of liability (§ 15.3)** — critical. The cap is 3% of bill-of-materials value over the whole term (far below a 12-month fees measure) and there are **no carve-outs at all**, so MSL's § 15.1 indemnities, confidentiality breaches, gross negligence and wilful misconduct all sit inside that 3%. This is the priority redline.
2. **Assignment (§ 16.2)** — high. Flat mutual consent with no affiliate/successor carve-out for us and no reasonableness standard on the consent we must obtain. (§ 16.5 Sale or Merger is favourable to us and stays.)
3. **Termination for convenience (§ 4.0 / § 5.0)** — high. A fixed three-year term with cause-only exit; PO-level cancellation under SOW § 6.1 mitigates but is not an Agreement-level exit.
4. **Auto-renewal (§ 4.0; SOW § 2.0)** — medium. Non-renewal notice of six months (Base Agreement) and twelve months for six-month renewal periods (SOW), i.e. notice due before the renewal period begins.
5. **Non-solicitation (§ 9.0(f))** — medium. Scope and carve-outs are acceptable; duration is a redacted multi-year period exceeding our 12-month limit.
6. **Insurance** — missing. No CGL, professional liability or cyber cover anywhere; only narrow consigned-inventory and tooling property cover.

Several figures are redacted ([*]) in our copy and must be confirmed against the unredacted version (see Next steps).

---

## 2. Findings table

| Severity | Rule | Status | Section | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Critical | LOL-CAP — Limitation of liability: cap, mutuality, carve-outs | **Deviation** | § 15.3 Limitations of Liability | Cap = 3% of bill-of-materials value over the term; no carve-outs. Mutuality satisfied. |
| Critical | INDEMN — Indemnification by Vendor | Compliant | § 15.1 Scope of MSL's Indemnity | Meets and substantially exceeds preferred; § 15.3(b) cap bites on it, addressed under LOL-CAP. |
| Critical | IP — Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data | Compliant | § 13.0 Intellectual and Industrial Property | Ownership vests in us; exceeds preferred position. |
| High | ASSIGN — Assignment and change of control | **Deviation** | § 16.2 Assignment | No affiliate/successor carve-out for us; no reasonableness standard on our consent. |
| High | T4C — Termination for convenience | **Deviation** | § 4.0 Term (with § 5.0/5.1) | Fixed three-year term, cause-only exit; no mid-term convenience right. |
| High | EXCLUSIVITY — Exclusivity binding Customer | Compliant | § 6.0 Purchase of Products | No exclusivity or requirements commitment on us. |
| High | LD — Liquidated damages/penalties payable by Customer | Compliant | § 6.1 Cancellation of Purchase Order | No LDs or early-termination fees on us; penalty mechanics run against MSL. |
| High | LICENSE — Licence grant scope | Compliant | § 13.0 Intellectual and Industrial Property | All grants run from us to MSL; ownership better than a licence. |
| High | NONCOMPETE — Non-compete restrictions on Customer | Compliant | § 14.18 Restrictions and Limitations | No restriction on our business; use restrictions bind MSL. |
| Medium | RENEWAL — Auto-renewal and non-renewal notice window | **Deviation** | § 4.0 Term (and SOW § 2.0) | Six-month and twelve-month notice windows; no renewal price cap. |
| Medium | NOSOLICIT — Non-solicitation binding Customer | **Deviation** | § 9.0 Personnel | Duration "[*] years" from Effective Date exceeds 12 months; scope/carve-outs acceptable. |
| Medium | AUDIT — Audit rights against Customer | Compliant | § 7.0 Audit | All audit rights run in our favour; no reciprocal right against us. |
| Medium | GOVLAW — Governing law and venue | Compliant | § 16.9 Governing Law | New York law and New York courts; no arbitration clause. |
| Medium | MFN — MFN obligations burdening Customer | Compliant | Attachment 1 | Only MFN runs in our favour ("most favored customer" engineering pricing). |
| Medium | MINCOMMIT — Minimum purchase commitments/volume restrictions | Compliant | § 6.0 Purchase of Products | No take-or-pay; Appendix 2 accuracy true-up noted in diligence only. |
| Medium | TRANSITION — Post-termination assistance and data return | Compliant | § 5.2 Rights Upon Termination | Uncapped exit assistance plus return obligations; return period redacted. |
| Medium | WARRANTY — Performance warranty and duration | Compliant | § 19.1 Scope of Warranty | Express conformance/workmanship warranty, repair-replace-refund, epidemic failure; periods redacted. |
| Low | INSURANCE — Vendor insurance | **Missing** | § 13.1 Consigned Products (only related cover) | No CGL, professional liability or cyber cover; fallback not met on any term. |

---

## 3. Walk-away items

The following sit in walk-away territory under the playbook and should be treated as conditions of signature:

1. **§ 15.3(b) liability cap with no carve-outs.** MSL's indemnities, confidentiality breaches, gross negligence and wilful misconduct capped at 3% of bill-of-materials value. Position: reset the cap to the greater of 12 months' amounts paid or payable and US$1,000,000, and add an Excluded Claims sentence covering indemnities, confidentiality, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud and IP infringement. The clause stays mutual.
2. **§ 16.2 blanket assignment consent.** A prohibition on our assignment with no M&A carve-out is the walk-away case. Position: add an affiliate/successor carve-out on written notice plus a reasonableness standard, leaving MSL's restrictions and subcontracting notice duties intact; § 16.5 is confirmed unchanged for the avoidance of doubt.
3. **No termination for convenience during a three-year term.** Position: add a convenience right for us on 30 days' notice with refund of prepaid amounts, preserving the §§ 5.2/5.3 wind-down and pricing bargain; confirm MSL has no convenience right.
4. **Non-renewal notice windows beyond 90 days (§ 4.0; SOW § 2.0).** Position: shorten notice to 30 days, align renewal periods at 12 months, add a 60-day renewal reminder and a lesser-of-CPI-or-3% uplift cap. Fallback: 60-day window with a 5% cap.
5. **Absence of any liability insurance.** MSL occupies our premises, handles our and our customers' inventory and accesses our I/T systems. Position: new § 16.22 requiring CGL, professional liability, cyber and workers' compensation cover at preferred limits, with certificates on request and existing consigned-inventory and tooling cover preserved. Fallback: E&O US$1M / cyber US$2M.

**Conditional:** the § 9.0(f) non-solicit becomes a walk-away item only if the redacted period exceeds 24 months. Our redline resets it to 12 months, with an 18-month landing zone available.

---

## 4. Next steps

1. **Issue the redline** on the five deviations plus the new insurance section, leading with § 15.3 and § 16.2 as the non-negotiables and holding the stated fallbacks in reserve.
2. **Obtain the unredacted figures** and confirm each against the playbook: the "[*] years" non-solicit period (§ 9.0(f)); the "[*] Days" confidential-information return period in § 5.2(a)(iii) (we revisit if materially longer than 30 days); the MSL Procured Parts and workmanship warranty periods and the § 16.19 survival cut-off (SOW § 19.1); and the Appendix 2 / § 13.0(f) requirements-accuracy percentages.
3. **Commercial sign-off** from the sourcing team on the Appendix 2 forecast-accuracy true-up percentages — noted as reliance-based reimbursement rather than take-or-pay, but the economics should be modelled before signature.
4. **Do not reopen** the compliant clauses. IP ownership (§ 13.0), the MSL indemnity (§ 15.1), warranty (SOW § 19), audit (§ 7.0), transition (§ 5.2) and the absence of exclusivity, MFN, minimum-volume and LD exposure all run in our favour; the only sub-elements short of preferred wording (no affiliate extension on the indemnity, no machine-readable-format or all-systems deletion certification on data return, no express services or no-malicious-code warranty, non-exclusive venue wording) are noted for the record and not pursued.
5. **Confirm on close** that no side letter or purchase-order terms reintroduce exclusivity, minimum volumes or a reciprocal audit or non-solicit obligation on us."}

## 3. Walk-away items

The following sit in walk-away territory under the playbook and should be treated as conditions of signature:

1. **§ 15.3(b) liability cap with no carve-outs.** MSL's indemnities, confidentiality breaches, gross negligence and wilful misconduct capped at 3% of bill-of-materials value. Position: reset the cap to the greater of 12 months' amounts paid or payable and US$1,000,000, and add an Excluded Claims sentence covering indemnities, confidentiality, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud and IP infringement. The clause stays mutual.
2. **§ 16.2 blanket assignment consent.** A prohibition on our assignment with no M&A carve-out is the walk-away case. Position: add an affiliate/successor carve-out on written notice plus a reasonableness standard, leaving MSL's restrictions and subcontracting notice duties intact; § 16.5 is confirmed unchanged for the avoidance of doubt.
3. **No termination for convenience during a three-year term.** Position: add a convenience right for us on 30 days' notice with refund of prepaid amounts, preserving the §§ 5.2/5.3 wind-down and pricing bargain; confirm MSL has no convenience right.
4. **Non-renewal notice windows beyond 90 days (§ 4.0; SOW § 2.0).** Position: shorten notice to 30 days, align renewal periods at 12 months, add a 60-day renewal reminder and a lesser-of-CPI-or-3% uplift cap. Fallback: 60-day window with a 5% cap.
5. **Absence of any liability insurance.** MSL occupies our premises, handles our and our customers' inventory and accesses our I/T systems. Position: new § 16.22 requiring CGL, professional liability, cyber and workers' compensation cover at preferred limits, with certificates on request and existing consigned-inventory and tooling cover preserved. Fallback: E&O US$1M / cyber US$2M.

**Conditional:** the § 9.0(f) non-solicit becomes a walk-away item only if the redacted period exceeds 24 months. Our redline resets it to 12 months, with an 18-month landing zone available.
